correctness.rationale: The domain and degree normalization are exact. The effective-resistance Kemeny sum follows from commute times. A cycle voltage and a Sherman–Morrison update give an explicit weighted potential variance and closed rational difference. Negative value at r=2(n-2), strict decrease of the numerator and full rational quotient, and opposite-chord asymptotics prove all quantifiers. Standalone independent exact Laplacian inversion verified all 100 chord cases for n<=22; this is supplementary to the infinite proof. Individual hitting times and spectral gap are not asserted.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Generic Kemeny forest and resistance identities apply to every graph but do not give the evaluated chord-separation sign, strict optimizer, or sharp asymptotic constant without additional specialized summation. The 2016 studied changes begin at trees, while 2026 sources treat twin/pendant clique settings and Erdős–Rényi asymptotics, not deterministic one-chord cycles.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A chorded cycle is a three-path theta graph with path lengths 1, d and n-d. The search therefore checked both descriptions and the stationary-target/random-walk formulations. Kirkland–Zeng use the ordinary cycle in a lollipop comparison and derive general forest formulas but do not compute the theta(1,d,n-d) chord insertion law; the other examined works do not do so either.

value.rationale: This is a natural minimal-edge-shortcut network transport problem, giving a complete exact placement classification for all cycles and an optimal 25% leading-order stationary-target hitting-time reduction. The strict no-Braess property on cycles contrasts with established tree Braess examples and is not a mere isolated computed invariant; the claimed value is the sharp structural optimization, not a generic resistance identity.
